sanskrit: yathārṣeṇeha vidhinā caratāvamatena ha mayādityād avāptāni yajūṃṣi mithilādhipa
english: By following here the ancient seers' ordinance, even one held in disregard, I obtained the Yajus verses from the Sun himself, O lord of Mithilā.

sanskrit: mahatā tapasā devas tapiṣṭhaḥ sevito mayā prītena cāhaṃ vibhunā sūryeṇoktas tadānagha
english: With great austerity I served the god of fiercest heat; and well pleased, the all-pervading Sūrya then spoke to me, O sinless one.

sanskrit: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva viprarṣe yad iṣṭaṃ te sudurlabham tat te dāsyāmi prītātmā matprasādo hi durlabhaḥ
english: "Choose a boon, O sage among brāhmaṇas, whatever you desire, however hard to win; that I shall grant you with a gladdened heart, for my favor is hard to obtain."

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇamya śirasā mayoktas tapatāṃ varaḥ yajūṃṣi nopayuktāni kṣipram icchāmi veditum
english: Then, bowing my head, I said to the best of those who give heat: "The Yajus verses not yet possessed — these I wish to learn quickly."

sanskrit: tato māṃ bhagavān āha vitariṣyāmi te dvija sarasvatīha vāgbhūtā śarīraṃ te pravekṣyati
english: Then the Blessed One said to me: "I shall impart them to you, O brāhmaṇa; Sarasvatī, become speech, will enter into your body."

sanskrit: tato mām āha bhagavān āsyaṃ svaṃ vivṛtaṃ kuru vivṛtaṃ ca tato me ''syaṃ praviṣṭā ca sarasvatī
english: Then the Blessed One said to me: "Open wide your mouth." And when I had opened my mouth, Sarasvatī entered it.

sanskrit: tato vidahyamāno 'haṃ praviṣṭo 'mbhas tadānagha avijñānād amarṣāc ca bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, burning, I plunged into the water, O sinless one, out of ignorance and impatience toward the great-souled maker of light.

sanskrit: tato vidahyamānaṃ mām uvāca bhagavān raviḥ muhūrtaṃ sahyatāṃ dāhas tataḥ śītībhaviṣyasi
english: Then, as I burned, the Blessed Sun said to me: "Bear the burning for a moment, and thereafter you shall become cool."

sanskrit: śītībhūtaṃ ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavān āha bhāskaraḥ pratiṣṭhāsyati te vedaḥ sottaraḥ sakhilo dvija
english: And seeing me grown cool, the Blessed maker of light said: "The Veda, with its supplements and its appendices, shall be established in you, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛtsnaṃ śatapathaṃ caiva praṇeṣyasi dvijarṣabha tasyānte cāpunarbhāve buddhis tava bhaviṣyati
english: And you shall set forth the whole of the Śatapatha, O bull among brāhmaṇas; and at its end your mind shall be set upon nonrebirth.

sanskrit: prāpsyase ca yad iṣṭaṃ tat sāṃkhyayogepsitaṃ padam etāvad uktvā bhagavān astam evābhyavartata
english: And you shall attain what you desire, that state sought by the followers of Sāṃkhya and Yoga." Having said only this much, the Blessed One went to his setting.

sanskrit: tato 'nuvyāhṛtaṃ śrutvā gate deve vibhāvasau gṛham āgatya saṃhṛṣṭo 'cintayaṃ vai sarasvatīm
english: Then, having heard what was declared, when the radiant god had departed, I returned home and, full of joy, I meditated upon Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttātiśubhā svaravyañjanabhūṣitā oṃkāram āditaḥ kṛtvā mama devī sarasvatī
english: Then the goddess Sarasvatī came forth in me, most auspicious, adorned with vowels and consonants, making the syllable Oṃ at the beginning.

sanskrit: tato 'ham arghyaṃ vidhivat sarasvatyai nyavedayam tapatāṃ ca variṣṭhāya niṣaṇṇas tatparāyaṇaḥ
english: Then I duly offered the guest-water to Sarasvatī and to the most excellent of those who give heat, seated and wholly devoted to them.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatapathaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sarahasyaṃ sasaṃgraham cakre sapariśeṣaṃ ca harṣeṇa parameṇa ha
english: Then I composed the whole Śatapatha, with its esoteric portions, its compendium, and its appendices, with the utmost delight.

sanskrit: kṛtvā cādhyayanaṃ teṣāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ śatam uttamam vipriyārthaṃ saśiṣyasya mātulasya mahātmanaḥ
english: And having taught it, I produced a hundred excellent disciples — to the displeasure of my great-souled maternal uncle and his pupils.

sanskrit: tataḥ saśiṣyeṇa mayā sūryeṇeva gabhastibhiḥ vyāpto yajño mahārāja pitus tava mahātmanaḥ
english: Then by me together with my disciples, as the Sun pervades with his rays, the sacrifice of your great-souled father was overspread, O great king.

sanskrit: miṣato devalasyāpi tato 'rdhaṃ hṛtavān aham svavedadakṣiṇāyātha vimarde mātulena ha
english: Then, even as Devala looked on, I carried off half the sacrificial fee due to my own Veda, in contest with my maternal uncle.

sanskrit: sumantunātha pailena tathā jaimininā ca vai pitrā te munibhiś caiva tato 'ham anumānitaḥ
english: Then by Sumantu, by Paila, by Jaimini, by your father, and by the sages, I was honored and acknowledged.

sanskrit: daśa pañca ca prāptāni yajūṃṣy arkān mayānagha tathaiva lomaharṣāc ca purāṇam avadhāritam
english: Fifteen Yajus recensions I obtained from the Sun, O sinless one; and likewise from Lomaharṣaṇa the Purāṇa lore was ascertained.

sanskrit: bījam etat puraskṛtya devīṃ caiva sarasvatīm sūryasya cānubhāvena pravṛtto 'haṃ narādhipa
english: Placing this seed before me, and the goddess Sarasvatī, and by the power of the Sun, I set to work, O ruler of men,

sanskrit: kartuṃ śatapathaṃ vedam apūrvaṃ kāritaṃ ca me yathābhilaṣitaṃ mārgaṃ tathā tac copapāditam
english: to compose the Śatapatha Veda, never before made; and it was brought about by me, accomplished in the manner I had wished.

sanskrit: śiṣyāṇām akhilaṃ kṛtsnam anujñātaṃ sasaṃgraham sarve ca śiṣyāḥ śucayo gatāḥ paramaharṣitāḥ
english: To my disciples the whole of it entire, together with its compendium, was imparted; and all the disciples, pure, departed in supreme delight.

sanskrit: śākhāḥ pañcadaśemās tu vidyā bhāskaradarśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpya yathākāmaṃ vedyaṃ tad anucintayam
english: Having established at will these fifteen branches of lore shown by the maker of light, I then pondered upon that which is to be known:

sanskrit: kim atra brahmaṇyam ṛtaṃ kiṃ ca vedyam anuttamam cintaye tatra cāgatya gandharvo mām apṛcchata
english: "What here is the holy truth, and what is the supreme object of knowledge?" As I was reflecting on this, a gandharva came and questioned me —

sanskrit: viśvāvasus tato rājan vedāntajñānakovidaḥ caturviṃśatikān praśnān pṛṣṭvā vedasya pārthiva pañcaviṃśatimaṃ praśnaṃ papracchānvīkṣikīṃ tathā
english: Viśvāvasu, O king, skilled in the knowledge of the Vedānta; having asked twenty-four questions about the Veda, O lord of the earth, he asked a twenty-fifth question, concerning the science of reasoning.

sanskrit: viśvāviśvaṃ tathāśvāśvaṃ mitraṃ varuṇam eva ca jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ tathājño jñaḥ kas tapā atapās tathā sūryādaḥ sūrya iti ca vidyāvidye tathaiva ca
english: The universal and the non-universal; the pervading and the unpervading; Mitra and Varuṇa; knowledge and the knowable; the unknowing and the knowing; who is the warm and the not-warm; the devourer of the Sun and the Sun; knowledge and ignorance, likewise;

sanskrit: vedyāvedyaṃ tathā rājann acalaṃ calam eva ca apūrvam akṣayaṃ kṣayyam etat praśnam anuttamam
english: the knowable and the unknowable, O king; the unmoving and the moving; the unprecedented, the imperishable, and the perishable — this was that incomparable question.

sanskrit: athoktaś ca mayā rājan rājā gandharvasattamaḥ pṛṣṭavān anupūrveṇa praśnam uttamam arthavat
english: Then I addressed him, O king — that king among gandharvas — who had asked, in due order, a question lofty and full of meaning:

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ mṛṣyatāṃ tāvad yāvad enaṃ vicintaye bāḍham ity eva kṛtvā sa tūṣṇīṃ gandharva āsthitaḥ
english: "Let it be borne with for a moment, until I reflect upon it." Saying "So be it," the gandharva remained silent.

sanskrit: tato 'nvacintayam ahaṃ bhūyo devīṃ sarasvatīm manasā sa ca me praśno dadhno ghṛtam ivoddhṛtam
english: Then once more I called to mind the goddess Sarasvatī; and in my mind that question was churned out, as clarified butter is drawn from curds.

sanskrit: tatropaniṣadaṃ caiva pariśeṣaṃ ca pārthiva mathnāmi manasā tāta dṛṣṭvā cānvīkṣikīṃ parām
english: There I churned, in my mind, both the Upaniṣad and the appendix, O son, having beheld the supreme science of reasoning.

sanskrit: caturthī rājaśārdūla vidyaiṣā sāṃparāyikī udīritā mayā tubhyaṃ pañcaviṃśe 'dhi dhiṣṭhitā
english: This, O tiger among kings, is the fourth science, that which avails for the world beyond; it was declared by me to you, founded upon the twenty-fifth principle.

sanskrit: athoktas tu mayā rājan rājā viśvāvasus tadā śrūyatāṃ yad bhavān asmān praśnaṃ saṃpṛṣṭavān iha
english: Then I addressed him, O king — King Viśvāvasu — at that time: "Hear now the answer to the question you have here asked of me."

sanskrit: viśvāviśveti yad idaṃ gandharvendrānupṛcchasi viśvāvyaktaṃ paraṃ vidyād bhūtabhavyabhayaṃkaram
english: "As for this universal and non-universal about which you inquire, O lord of gandharvas, let one know the supreme Unmanifest as the universal, the dread of all that has been and shall be.

sanskrit: triguṇaṃ guṇakartṛtvād aviśvo niṣkalas tathā aśvas tathaiva mithunam evam evānudṛśyate
english: It is threefold through the agency of the qualities; the non-universal, again, is the partless one. The 'pervading' is likewise seen as a pair, even so.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ prakṛtiṃ prāhuḥ puruṣeti ca nirguṇam tathaiva mitraṃ puruṣaṃ varuṇaṃ prakṛtiṃ tathā
english: They call the Unmanifest Prakṛti, and the quality-less they call Puruṣa; likewise Mitra is the Puruṣa, and Varuṇa is Prakṛti.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ tu prakṛtiṃ prāhur jñeyaṃ niṣkalam eva ca ajñaś ca jñaś ca puruṣas tasmān niṣkala ucyate
english: Knowledge they call Prakṛti, and the knowable is the partless one; the Puruṣa is both unknowing and knowing, and therefore he is called partless.

sanskrit: kas tapā atapāḥ proktaḥ ko 'sau puruṣa ucyate tapāḥ prakṛtir ity āhur atapā niṣkalaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Who is the warm, who is called the not-warm, and who is he said to be the Puruṣa? The warm, they say, is Prakṛti; the not-warm is held to be the partless one.

sanskrit: tathaivāvedyam avyaktaṃ vedyaḥ puruṣa ucyate calācalam iti proktaṃ tvayā tad api me śṛṇu
english: So too the Unmanifest is the unknowable, while the Puruṣa is called the knowable. As for the 'moving and unmoving' you have spoken of, hear that also from me.

sanskrit: calāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ prāhuḥ kāraṇaṃ kṣepasargayoḥ akṣepasargayoḥkartā niścalaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: They call Prakṛti the moving, the cause of casting forth and creation; the Puruṣa, who neither casts forth nor creates, is held to be the unmoving.

sanskrit: ajāv ubhāv aprajau ca akṣayau cāpy ubhāv api ajau nityāv ubhau prāhur adhyātmagatiniścayāḥ
english: Both are unborn and offspringless, and both also imperishable; both, they say, are unborn and eternal — those who are firm in the knowledge of the higher Self.

sanskrit: akṣayatvāt prajanane ajam atrāhur avyayam akṣayaṃ puruṣaṃ prāhuḥ kṣayo hy asya na vidyate
english: Because it is imperishable in begetting, they call it here unborn and undecaying; the Puruṣa they call imperishable, for no decay is found in him.

sanskrit: guṇakṣayatvāt prakṛtiḥ kartṛtvād akṣayaṃ budhāḥ eṣā te ''nvīkṣikī vidyā caturthī sāṃparāyikī
english: Because of the perishing of its qualities it is Prakṛti; yet because it is the agent, the wise call it imperishable. This is for you the science of reasoning, the fourth, which avails for the world beyond.

sanskrit: vidyopetaṃ dhanaṃ kṛtvā karmaṇā nityakarmaṇi ekāntadarśanā vedāḥ sarve viśvāvaso smṛtāḥ
english: Having made wealth endowed with knowledge by action in the perpetual rite — all the Vedas are held to be of single, definite vision, O Viśvāvasu.

sanskrit: jāyante ca mriyante ca yasminn ete yataś cyutāḥ vedārthaṃ ye na jānanti vedyaṃ gandharvasattama
english: They who do not know the purpose of the Veda — that wherein these beings are born and die, and whence they have fallen — they do not know the knowable, O best of gandharvas.

sanskrit: sāṅgopāṅgān api yadi pañca vedān adhīyate vedavedyaṃ na jānīte vedabhāravaho hi saḥ
english: Even if one studies the five Vedas with all their limbs and sub-limbs, yet does not know what the Veda is to make known, he is but a bearer of the Veda's burden.

sanskrit: yo ghṛtārthī kharīkṣīraṃ mathed gandharvasattama viṣṭhāṃ tatrānupaśyeta na maṇḍaṃ nāpi vā ghṛtam
english: He who, desiring butter, should churn the milk of a she-ass, O best of gandharvas, would find there only dung — neither cream nor butter.

sanskrit: tathā vedyam avedyaṃ ca vedavidyo na vindati sa kevalaṃ mūḍhamatir jñānabhāravahaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Even so, one who knows the Veda's letter does not find the knowable and the unknowable; he, of merely deluded mind, is held a bearer of the burden of knowledge.

sanskrit: draṣṭavyau nityam evaitau tatpareṇāntarātmanā yathāsya janmanidhane na bhavetāṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: These two are ever to be discerned, by the inner Self devoted to that supreme end, so that for him birth and death may not be, again and again.

sanskrit: ajasraṃ janmanidhanaṃ cintayitvā trayīm imām parityajya kṣayam iha akṣayaṃ dharmam āsthitaḥ
english: Having pondered the ceaseless round of birth and death, and abandoning this triple Veda — which is here perishable — one takes his stand upon the imperishable dharma.

sanskrit: yadā tu paśyate 'tyantam ahany ahani kāśyapa tadā sa kevalībhūtaḥ ṣaḍviṃśam anupaśyati
english: But when, O Kāśyapa, he sees utterly, day after day, then, become wholly isolated, he beholds the twenty-sixth.

sanskrit: anyaś ca śaśvad avyaktas tathānyaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ tasya dvāv anupaśyeta tam ekam iti sādhavaḥ
english: One is the ever-Unmanifest, and other is the twenty-fifth; though there be these two of his, the good behold him as one alone.

sanskrit: tenaitan nābhijānanti pañcaviṃśakam acyutam janmamṛtyubhayād yogāḥ sāṃkhyāś ca paramaiṣiṇaḥ
english: For this reason they do not recognize the twenty-fifth as imperishable — the followers of Yoga and Sāṃkhya, seekers of the highest, dreading birth and death.

sanskrit: viśvāvasur uvāca pañcaviṃśaṃ yad etat te proktaṃ brāhmaṇasattama tathā tan na tathā veti tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Viśvāvasu said: As for this twenty-fifth that has been declared by you, O best of brāhmaṇas — whether it is so or not so, it behooves you to tell.

sanskrit: jaigīṣavyasyāsitasya devalasya ca me śrutam parāśarasya viprarṣer vārṣagaṇyasya dhīmataḥ
english: I have heard the teaching of Jaigīṣavya, of Asita, and of Devala; of the sage Parāśara, and of the wise Vārṣagaṇya;

sanskrit: bhikṣoḥ pañcaśikhasyātha kapilasya śukasya ca gautamasyārṣṭiṣeṇasya gargasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: of the mendicant Pañcaśikha, of Kapila and Śuka, of Gautama, of Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, and of the great-souled Garga;

sanskrit: nāradasyāsureś caiva pulastyasya ca dhīmataḥ sanatkumārasya tataḥ śukrasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: of Nārada and of Āsuri, and of the wise Pulastya; of Sanatkumāra, then, and of the great-souled Śukra;

sanskrit: kaśyapasya pituś caiva pūrvam eva mayā śrutam tadanantaraṃ ca rudrasya viśvarūpasya dhīmataḥ
english: of Kaśyapa and of my own father, all this I heard long ago; and thereafter of Rudra of universal form, the wise one,

sanskrit: daivatebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaś ca daityebhyaś ca tatas tataḥ prāptam etan mayā kṛtsnaṃ vedyaṃ nityaṃ vadanty uta
english: and from the gods, the ancestors, and the daityas, here and there; all this has been gained by me — what they ever call the knowable, the eternal.

sanskrit: tasmāt tad vai bhavadbuddhyā śrotum icchāmi brāhmaṇa bhavān prabarhaḥ śāstrāṇāṃ pragalbhaś cātibuddhimān
english: Therefore I wish to hear it through your understanding, O brāhmaṇa; you are the foremost of the treatises, bold and of surpassing intellect.

sanskrit: na tavāviditaṃ kiṃ cid bhavāñ śrutinidhiḥ smṛtaḥ kathyate devaloke ca pitṛloke ca brāhmaṇa
english: Nothing is unknown to you; you are held to be a treasury of sacred lore, O brāhmaṇa — so it is told in the world of the gods and in the world of the ancestors.

sanskrit: brahmalokagatāś caiva kathayanti maharṣayaḥ patiś ca tapatāṃ śaśvad ādityas tava bhāṣate
english: The great sages who have gone to the world of Brahmā recount it, and the lord of those who give heat, the Sun himself, ever speaks of you.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyajñānaṃ tvayā brahmann avāptaṃ kṛtsnam eva ca tathaiva yogajñānaṃ ca yājñavalkya viśeṣataḥ
english: The knowledge of Sāṃkhya has been obtained by you whole and entire, O brāhmaṇa, and likewise the knowledge of Yoga in particular, O Yājñavalkya.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃdigdhaṃ prabuddhas tvaṃ budhyamānaś carācaram śrotum icchāmi taj jñānaṃ ghṛtaṃ maṇḍamayaṃ yathā
english: Beyond all doubt you are awakened, comprehending the moving and the unmoving; I wish to hear that knowledge, even as one would the cream-rich butter.

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca kṛtsnadhāriṇam eva tvāṃ manye gandharvasattama jijñāsasi ca māṃ rājaṃs tan nibodha yathāśrutam
english: Yājñavalkya said: I deem you to be one who has grasped the whole, O best of gandharvas; yet you would test me, O king. Learn it, then, as I have heard it.

sanskrit: abudhyamānāṃ prakṛtiṃ budhyate pañcaviṃśakaḥ na tu budhyati gandharva prakṛtiḥ pañcaviṃśakam
english: The twenty-fifth knows Prakṛti, who herself does not know; but Prakṛti, O gandharva, does not know the twenty-fifth.

sanskrit: anenāpratibodhena pradhānaṃ pravadanti tam sāṃkhyayogāś ca tattvajñā yathāśrutinidarśanāt
english: Because of this non-awareness they call her the Pradhāna — both the Sāṃkhyas and the Yogas, knowers of the truth, according to the testimony of scripture.

sanskrit: paśyaṃs tathaivāpaśyaṃś ca paśyaty anyas tathānagha ṣaḍviṃśaḥ pañcaviṃśaṃ ca caturviṃśaṃ ca paśyati na tu paśyati paśyaṃs tu yaś cainam anupaśyati
english: Seeing and likewise not-seeing, yet another one sees, O sinless one: the twenty-sixth sees both the twenty-fifth and the twenty-fourth; but, though seeing, the one he sees does not see him in return.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśo 'bhimanyeta nānyo 'sti paramo mama na caturviṃśako 'grāhyo manujair jñānadarśibhiḥ
english: The twenty-fifth would imagine: "There is no other higher than I" — yet the twenty-fourth is not ungraspable to men who behold by knowledge.

sanskrit: matsyevodakam anveti pravartati pravartanāt yathaiva budhyate matsyas tathaiṣo 'py anubudhyate sasnehaḥ sahavāsāc ca sābhimānaś ca nityaśaḥ
english: As a fish follows the water and moves by reason of its movement, even as the fish has awareness, so too does this one come to awareness — bound by affection, by shared dwelling, and ever by self-conceit.

sanskrit: sa nimajjati kālasya yadaikatvaṃ na budhyate unmajjati hi kālasya mamatvenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: He sinks in time when he does not comprehend his oneness; and he rises in time, enveloped by the sense of "mine."

sanskrit: yadā tu manyate 'nyo 'ham anya eṣa iti dvijaḥ tadā sa kevalībhūtaḥ ṣaḍviṃśam anupaśyati
english: But when the twice-born thinks, "I am other, and this is other," then, become wholly isolated, he beholds the twenty-sixth.

sanskrit: anyaś ca rājann avaras tathānyaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ tatsthatvād anupaśyanti eka eveti sādhavaḥ
english: One, O king, is the lower, and other is the twenty-fifth; yet because the one abides within the other, the good behold them as one alone.

sanskrit: tenaitan nābhinandanti pañcaviṃśakam acyutam janmamṛtyubhayād bhītā yogāḥ sāṃkhyāś ca kāśyapa ṣaḍviṃśam anupaśyanti śucayas tatparāyaṇāḥ
english: For this reason they do not delight in the twenty-fifth as imperishable; afraid of the dread of birth and death, the Yogas and the Sāṃkhyas, O Kāśyapa, the pure and wholly devoted, behold the twenty-sixth.

sanskrit: yadā sa kevalībhūtaḥ ṣaḍviṃśam anupaśyati tadā sa sarvavid vidvān na punarjanma vindati
english: When, become wholly isolated, he beholds the twenty-sixth, then that learned one, all-knowing, does not undergo birth again.

sanskrit: evam apratibuddhaś ca budhyamānaś ca te 'nagha buddhaś cokto yathātattvaṃ mayā śrutinidarśanāt
english: Thus the unawakened, the awakening, and the awakened have been declared to you, O sinless one, according to their truth, by me, from the testimony of scripture.

sanskrit: paśyāpaśyaṃ yo 'nupaśyet kṣemaṃ tattvaṃ ca kāśyapa kevalākevalaṃ cādyaṃ pañcaviṃśāt paraṃ ca yat
english: Whoever should behold the seen and the unseen, O Kāśyapa, and the blissful Reality — the isolated and the non-isolated, the primal, and that which is beyond the twenty-fifth —

sanskrit: viśvāvasur uvāca tathyaṃ śubhaṃ caitad uktaṃ tvayā bhoḥ; samyak kṣemyaṃ devatādyaṃ yathāvat svasty akṣayaṃ bhavataś cāstu nityaṃ; buddhyā sadā buddhiyuktaṃ namas te
english: Viśvāvasu said: True and auspicious is this that has been spoken by you, sir — rightly, bringing peace, beginning with the deity, exactly so. May there be welfare imperishable to you for ever; ever joined with wisdom through your wisdom — homage to you!

sanskrit: yājñavalkya uvāca evam uktvā saṃprayāto divaṃ sa; vibhrājan vai śrīmatā darśanena tuṣṭaś ca tuṣṭyā parayābhinandya; pradakṣiṇaṃ mama kṛtvā mahātmā
english: Yājñavalkya said: Having spoken thus, he set forth to heaven, shining indeed with a glorious aspect; and well content, with the highest contentment, that great-souled one rejoiced and made his rightward circuit around me.
